title: pothos agent contract
description: Tells the pothos skills how this repository is verified, run and documented. Private to each developer: stored under ~/.config/pothos/contracts/<host>/<owner>/<repo>.json, never inside the repository.

version.description: Contract format version. Bumped only on breaking changes. Migrating older contracts is planned for plant's audit mode.

workflow.description: Who owns the development cycle in this repository. pothos (default): the pothos skills run the cycle. repo: the repository's own workflow applies, pothos's cycle skills stand aside and point to it, and hooks stay silent. Knowledge skills still apply.

verify.description: Shell commands, run from the repository root. Each must exit 0 when the change is good. Required unless workflow is repo. A missing e2e means the repo has no end-to-end suite yet: skills skip that check and report it, never improvise one.

fast.description: Seconds-range check for quick feedback after edits, e.g. type-check plus lint. A Stop hook that runs it is planned.

full.description: Everything CI checks before merge. verify runs it, and nothing merges without a green run on the current commit.

e2e.description: End-to-end suite over the critical flows. Optional while the repo has none.

run.description: How an agent starts the app to look at a change.

setup.description: Command that prepares a fresh clone or worktree before anything else runs: install dependencies, generate code (ORM clients, API types). Implementers run it first in every new worktree.

dev.description: Starts the app against the default backend. Prefer a mode that needs no real backend or credentials.

mocked.description: true when run.dev works without a real backend or secrets.

login.description: Path to a doc that explains how an agent signs in to the running app.

environments.description: Backends the app can run against, when there is more than one. Before starting work on a feature, implement asks which one to use, because the choice usually depends on who you are working with.

dev.description: Command that starts the app against this backend.

e2e.description: Headless end-to-end command against this backend, when it differs from verify.e2e.

screenshots.description: Which screenshots evidence can take of the running app. web: a headless browser at run.url. ios-simulator: the booted iOS simulator. android-emulator: the running Android emulator, through adb. none: no screenshots; evidence goes straight to test output and real calls without trying. Unset means unknown: evidence tries once and suggests setting this field.

apps.description: Monorepos only: one entry per app a change can touch, with how to start it and show it. verify and run.setup stay at the top level because they cover the whole repository. evidence uses the entries whose path the change touches.

dev.description: Command, run from the repository root, that starts this app.

url.description: Where this app answers when it runs.

mocked.description: true when dev works without a real backend or secrets.

screenshots.description: Same as run.screenshots, for this app.

ui.description: This app's UI building blocks, same fields as the top-level ui. In a monorepo it replaces the top-level ui for files under the app's path.

components.description: Repository-relative folders that hold the shared components (design-system primitives, common UI). Look here before creating a component.

tokens.description: Repository-relative files or folders that define design tokens or the theme: colors, spacing, type scale, breakpoints.

icons.description: Package new code takes icons from, e.g. lucide-react. Set only when one icon set is the convention.

preview.description: Where components render in isolation, such as Storybook.

command.description: Command that starts the preview, taken from a declared script.

url.description: Where the preview answers when it runs.

docs.description: Repository-relative paths to the domain knowledge agents must read.

glossary.description: Ubiquitous-language glossary, usually GLOSSARY.md (older repos: CONTEXT.md).

prd.description: Directory where to-spec writes specs when the tracker is local.

tracker.description: Where specs and tickets live. to-spec and to-tickets write there; implement and implement-spec read from there. The SessionStart adapter hands it to every skill.

project.description: Project key or board identifier, e.g. a Jira key.

skill.description: Repository skill that knows the tracker's fields and templates. When set, every tracker operation goes through it.

path.description: For kind local: directory holding one folder per feature with spec.md and issues/NN-slug.md files. Usually .scratch.

labels.description: Label strings this tracker uses for the five triage roles, when they differ from the role names.

review.description: Extra review inputs. code-review reads the standards as documented coding standards; the skills run after it.

standards.description: Repository files that document coding standards beyond the ones code-review finds on its own, e.g. docs/conventions.md.

build.description: Inputs for writing code. Implementers load these repository skills before they write code (design rules, component conventions); review skills stay under review.

ui.description: Where this repository's UI building blocks live. Sessions get it before UI work, so new code reuses what exists instead of adding a second button or a raw color. Every field is optional; a missing field means nobody confirmed it, and skills skip what depends on it instead of guessing. In a monorepo, put each app's own ui in its run.apps entry; the top-level ui then covers the rest of the repository.

components.description: Repository-relative folders that hold the shared components (design-system primitives, common UI). Look here before creating a component.

tokens.description: Repository-relative files or folders that define design tokens or the theme: colors, spacing, type scale, breakpoints.

icons.description: Package new code takes icons from, e.g. lucide-react. Set only when one icon set is the convention.

preview.description: Where components render in isolation, such as Storybook.

command.description: Command that starts the preview, taken from a declared script.

url.description: Where the preview answers when it runs.

template.description: Path to the pull request body template.

evidence.description: Where screenshots go for the pull request. github-release: evidence.py upload adds them to a monthly prerelease of this GitHub repository (pr-evidence-YYYY-MM) and never deletes them, so old pull requests keep their images. Any other value is a command that receives the file paths and prints markdown to embed.

auto_merge.description: Lets tend's merge gate merge a pull request that a person gave this label, once every check is green, no review asks for changes and no thread is open. Without it, a person merges every pull request.

label.description: The label a person adds to a pull request to let it merge itself. Agents never add it.

method.description: How the gate merges. Default squash.
